newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Materials copper output to dip.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Materials copper output to dip.

text.p: Mitsubishi Materials Corp said on Tuesday it planned to produce slightly less refined copper in the half year to next March than it did in the same period the year before, while lead output was slated to edge higher and zinc output was to fall sharply.

Copper output was planned at 23,000 tonnes per month, down from actual monthly output of 24,195 tonnes in the year-ago period and original planned monthly output of 24,650 tonnes in April-September 1996.
Lead output was forecast at 4,100 tonnes per month, up from 3,854 tonnes in the half year to March 1996 and output of 4,000 tonnes it had planned in the April-September half year.

Zinc output was put at 1,372 tonnes per month in the half year ahead, off sharply from 6,538 tonnes per month in the year-ago period but a more modest decline from 1,506 tonnes it had planned for April-September 1996.
The decline was attributed to the closing earlier this year of the company's Akita zinc smelter.

Gold output in the half year to March 1997 was planned at 4.35 tonnes per month, up from 4.186 tonnes in the year-ago period but unchanged from 4.35 tonnes it planned for the April-September half year.
Silver production was seen at 30.5 tonnes per month, down from 36.328 tonnes produced in the year-ago period and 31.667 tonnes originally planned for the April-September half year.
